title: Psilocybin desynchronizes the human brain
post: Background: It remains unclear how human brain network changes relate to subjective and lasting effects of psychedelics. Methods: Here we tracked individual-specific brain changes with longitudinal precision functional mapping (roughly 18 magnetic resonance imaging visits per participant). Results: Performing a perceptual task reduced psilocybin-driven FC changes. Psilocybin caused persistent decrease in FC between the anterior hippocampus and default mode network, lasting for weeks. Conclusion: Persistent reduction of hippocampal-default mode network connectivity may represent a neuroanatomical and mechanistic correlate of the proplasticity and therapeutic effects of psychedelics.

title: Cortical depth EEG-fMRI at 7T: Experimental setup and analysis pipeline to elucidate generating mechanisms of alpha oscillations.
post: Background: Alpha band (8-13 Hz) electroencephalography (EEG) oscillations are central to cognition, but their generating mechanisms are poorly understood. Methods: Ultra-high-field (UHF, 7T) laminar functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) enables cortical depth resolved brain responses, and, combined with simultaneous EEG, offers new insight into human alpha generation mechanisms. Conclusion: In conclusion, we have established a method to non-invasively interrogate the origins of electrophysiological signals.

title: FDTest: Fluctuation-dissipation theorem as a test for memory effects in brain dynamics.
post: Background: A central challenge in neuroscience is to understand how the brain flexibly balances local and distributed information processing to support diverse cognitive and conscious states. Methods: Here we introduce the FDTest, a method for assessing local memory effects in multidimensional systems by measuring violations of a generalized Fluctuation-dissipation theorem (FDT). post: Background: Modeling the brain as a controllable structural network allows the estimation of the control energy (CE) required to reach functional states, where low-CE states are more accessible. post: Background: While there is evidence for efficacy of 5-HT 2A R targeting drugs in schizophrenia and other disorders, the impact of volinanserin on circuit-level brain function and connectivity remains unknown. Methods: Here, we test the impact of volinanserin on behaviours in mice relevant to a range of symptom domains in schizophrenia. title: Default Mode Network Modulation by Psychedelics: A Systematic Review
post: Background: Psychedelics are a unique class of drug that commonly produce vivid hallucinations as well as profound psychological and mystical experiences. Methods: To date, several studies have investigated how psychedelics modulate this network, but no comprehensive review, to our knowledge, has critically evaluated how major classical psychedelic agents-lysergic acid diethylamide, psilocybin, and ayahuasca-modulate the DMN. Results: Across psychedelics there is consistent acute disruption in resting state connectivity within the DMN and increased functional connectivity between canonical resting-state networks. Various models have been proposed to explain the cognitive mechanisms of psychedelics, and in one model DMN modulation is a central axiom. Conclusion: This article aims to provide the field with a comprehensive overview that can propel future research in such a way as to elucidate the neurocognitive mechanisms of psychedelics.

post: Aim: Here we show that continental-scale uplift and subsidence associated with long-wavelength dynamic topography12 due to mantle convection drove the formation and preservation of the Great Unconformity. Methods: Our models predict prolonged continental-scale Neoproterozoic uplift and long-term Phanerozoic subsidence for Laurentia, Baltica and North China. Results: The predicted prolonged continental uplift throughout Cryogenian times would have resulted in marked erosion due to the action of glaciers13. Conclusion: Our models predict cycles of dynamic topography that are broadly reflected in preserved sediment volume across continents1,14, and open new avenues for understanding the environments of Cambrian animal diversification.

title: Repeated prefrontal transcranial direct current stimulation improves behavioral regulation and modulates resting-state EEG microstate dynamics in young adults with problematic smartphone use: a randomized sham-controlled longitudinal study.

title: Gender differences in depressive-like behavior in Parkinson's disease.
post: Background: Although sex differences have been described in PD progression, the mechanisms underlying gender-specific susceptibility to depressive symptoms remain poorly understood. title: Endogenous suspension of phenomenal consciousness during extended cessation: Regional homogeneity analysis of multi-participant 7T fMRI of an advanced meditative endpoint.
post: Background: Extended cessation (EC) is a rare advanced meditative state characterized by the voluntary absence of reportable phenomenal experience, followed by reproducible aftereffects including immense mental clarity, equanimity, and peace. Methods: In a small-N case study (N = 3) using ultra-high-resolution 7T functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) with dense within-subject sampling, we quantified whole-brain activity and related it to chemoarchitecture and cognitive maps. Results: EC is marked by increased activity in unimodal sensory cortices and viscerosensory brainstem nuclei, and down-regulation in transmodal regions, subcortex and brainstem. Conclusion: These findings constrain prevailing theories of consciousness by demonstrating that loss of experience need not entail global neural suppression, and supports accounts emphasizing selective precision modulation and hierarchical decoupling.

title: Mechanism-guided generative chemistry yields distinct agonist-like and antagonist-like ligand populations for the serotonin 5-HT2A receptor
post: Background: Designing serotonin 5-HT2A receptor ligands with a specified functional direction is difficult because binding affinity, assay-derived mechanism labels, molecular properties and receptor conformation are only partially coupled. Methods

We developed a mechanism-guided generative chemistry workflow integrating curated ChEMBL data, scaffold-aware supervised learning, a recurrent SMILES prior, reinforcement learning, medicinal-chemistry prioritization, receptor-context docking, MM-GBSA rescoring and property-adjusted contact analysis.
